metadata.title: Nasdaq plunges 1,100 points over renewed rate hike concerns

content.text:
US stocks (^DJI, ^IXIC, ^GSPC) sink in Friday trading, the Nasdaq Composite leading losses and closing over 1,100 points lower (4.18%). The market is reacting to May's overwhelmingly positive labor data — 172,000 jobs added the US economy vs. estimates of 88,000 — raising investor concerns that the Federal Reserve may be inclined to hike interest rates.
Yahoo Finance Markets and Data Editor Jared Blikre breaks down the day's biggest market moves.
Deep in their red with the Nasdaq leading the losses here. Let's get to Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre with the recap. Jared.
That's right. Nasdaq composite down 1,121 points at the end of the day. That's down 4.2% and the chart shows the uh the damage here. You can see it closed pretty close to the lows of the day and we were never in the green and all of this is the fallout from that hot payrolls report that we got this morning. Sometimes good news is bad news, especially when it implies Fed rate hikes and not cuts.
Here's the Dow. started out barely in the green, end of the day down about 694 points, 1.35%. and then here's the S&P 500, uh ending with kind of a mix between gainers and losers here, but at the end of the day, the mega caps, those big stocks and especially chip stocks dragged it down 2.64%. Meanwhile, Russell 2000 down 3.5%, and I should mention that the Russell 2000, Nasdaq composite, Nasdaq 100 and XLK had their worst day since those post liberation day lows in April of last year.
Now let's move on here. We're going to take a look at the large cap sector action. Staples finished in the green up 1.77%. After that you got utilities, real estate, healthcare, financials in the green. Most of those defensive sectors, so don't get too excited about that. But the good news is we did have some green. Uh in a true market panic, all of this would be red. But the only underperformer here, the only stock or the only sector doing worse than the S&P 500 is XLK, that's tech, down 6.68% and uh another bad day for tech.
We can see that in the Nasdaq 100 here. Lots of dark red and a lot of these are semiconductor names. Some of them are software, but you can see the big ones, Nvidia down 6%, Broadcom down almost 8%, even Tesla down 6 and a half%. And when we dig into the semiconductor heat map, you can really see the carnage. Intel down 11%, applied materials down about 10, SanDisk 11, Marvel down 16%. So a lot of the biggest gainers recently are also the biggest losers today. That's a pretty common pattern uh when you see something at these elevated levels here.
In software land, we got Oracle uh leading down down about 10%, but a lot of these issues down 4, 5, 6, 7%. Not quite as much dark red as our semiconductor heat map, but still you can see some damage done. And then when we take a look at the Dow, we see a little bit more green and that's because we have some of those defensive sectors uh lifting it or at least not uh at least pairing some of those gains.
Procter & Gamble up 4%, best day in I think years. J&J up 2%, Visa up 1%, McDonald's up 2.6%. So those kind of trades kind of balancing things out, but you see Cisco down six, Caterpillar down four, Goldman Sachs down almost five. Well, that is kind of an ugly tape for the day.
Want to show you the leaders here. Um at the top, we only got a little bit of green, low volatility, regional banks and transportations. IYT actually hit a record high close to the open and it's still main uh managed to maintain some gains there, so a record close as well. But the worst off performer here is EWI. That is a a Korean ETF. Top two components are Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and so that explains the uh the carnage there. Chip stocks really bleeding in there, leading that lower down 14%.
Second up is the Sox down 10%, worst day for the chip chip index since uh April of last year. Then we got solar, Quantum, disruption, emerging markets, momentum, all those down 5 to 8%. So I ended with Bitcoin an hour ago. I'm going to do another Bitcoin end update here. Down 5 and a half% over the last 24 hours. It cracked 60,000 briefly, but it's back above now, but that's some trade you want to watch over the weekend guys.
